svg.text: Relay-driver board on perfboard — where everything sits
[GA6] 50 × 80 double-sided, 2.54 mm pitch: 31 × 18 holes, of which the outer ring is border — 29 × 16 usable (both sides counted 2026-11-05).
One MOSFET, four coils, four flyback diodes, the gate pulldown, and the E-stop sense divider. The schematic is a separate figure; this one is only about placement.

Q1 — the TAB is the DRAIN
G
D
S
PULLDOWN and SOURCE ground ONE HOLE APART
Your question: yes — but the Teensy’s ground reaches it through the STAR, not through a second wire
The MOSFET is a low-side switch, so its SOURCE is the board ground. The pulldown holds the gate low against that source, so
“3.3 V on the gate” and “0 V on the gate” only mean anything if the Teensy shares that same node. That part of your reading is exactly right.
What it must not be is a second ground WIRE. This board’s ground already returns to the star on the PWR terminal, carrying the
whole 600 mA of coil current. A second ground conductor up to the Teensy is a parallel path — a loop, which is what §3.5.3 forbids.
What you accept instead is the IR drop in that one wire: 600 mA × ~0.011 Ω (1.5 mm² over 1 m) ≈ 7 mV, against a worst-case
Vᵐₛ(th) of 1.0 V. 0.7 %. A single star ground is not a compromise here — it is simply right, and it is one wire fewer.
Why the pulldown lives HERE, beside the MOSFET, and not at the Teensy end
Because then a cut gate wire is still safe. That wire runs from the logic box to the power box. With the pulldown at the Teensy end,
unplugging it would leave the gate floating at the MOSFET — partial enhancement, relays chattering between STOCK and DBW.
With it on this board, a broken gate wire still leaves 10 kΩ tied across gate and source. Gate low. Coils dropped. STOCK.
And its ground lands one hole from the source’s. Across a soldered bus that drop is microvolts, so this is cheap insurance rather than a
live hazard — but it is the habit that stays correct the day someone rebuilds the same circuit with wire instead of a bus.
One thing this drawing changed: the Teensy terminal carries GATE + SENSE, not GATE + GND
The E-stop sense divider is on this board (R3/R4, tapped off the coil feed), and its output has to get back to a Teensy input — but
no terminal in the §3.5.4 count carried it. The same omission as the gate-out way found on 2026-11-05, one board over.
Swapping GND for SENSE on that block fixes both at once and leaves the count untouched at 12 per vehicle, 36 for the fleet: the
ground was never supposed to be there, and the sense line always was.
Build order — unchanged; the layout follows it
1. GND bus, GND spine, R1. Nothing else.
2. Meter gate-to-GND: 10 kΩ. No MOSFET to
confuse the reading, no coil to be damaged by it.
3. Q1, then R2, then the four diodes.
Every band at the +12 V bus — one reversed
diode is a short across the logic pack.
4. Terminals, then coils last. Drive the gate from
a bench 3.3 V and listen for four clicks.
5. R3/R4 last, and meter the sense node before
the wire goes near a pin — it starts at pack
volts and the Teensy 4.1 is not 5 V tolerant.
Reading the drawing
Thick coloured runs are bare tinned wire soldered
along the holes: three buses and the GND spine.
Thin runs are insulated hookup wire, 22–24 AWG.
Dashed means route it on the reverse side — it
passes under the TO-220 and you cannot solder it
afterwards.
Crossings are fine. The board is 양면 and the wire
is insulated. What is never fine is two leads in one
hole, which this script asserts rather than trusting
the eye.
No row to spare. Rows 2–17 are the whole usable
height: the GND bus is on the LAST usable row.
Mounting: a corner M3 is out — the corner hole is
1.9 mm from the side edge against an M3’s 1.6 mm
radius. Mid-edge on the long sides there is 3.4 mm.
